plates.side_label: KEPLER (1604) & DONDERS/SNELLEN (1862): CORNEA (~43 D) + LENS (~15–20 D) = ~58–60 D AT 24 MM AXIAL LENGTH (±1 MM = ∓3 DIOPTRES)
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Optics of the Human Eye, Retinal Inversion, Accommodation & Refractive Correction chart from Ibn al-Haytham (1011–1021 AD Kitāb al-Manāẓir / Book of Optics), Johannes Kepler (1604 Ad Vitellionem Paralipomena), Christoph Scheiner (1619 Oculus), Thomas Young (1801 Phil. Trans. R. Soc. 91: 23–88), and Franciscus Donders & Herman Snellen (1862 Probebuchstaben zur Bestimmung der Sehschärfe) shows 1) Camera obscura intromission rays crossing at the pupil/lens to form an inverted retinal image; 2) Ciliary muscle accommodation flattening the lens for distance vs fattening it for near vision; and 3) Concave (myopia), convex (hyperopia/presbyopia), and cylindrical (astigmatism) spectacle lenses + Snellen's 5-arcminute 20/20 optotype geometry.

teach_overlay.label: KEPLER (1604) & DONDERS/SNELLEN (1862) HUMAN EYE RAY-TRACING (~58–60 DIOPTRES AT 24 MM AXIAL LENGTH; ±1 MM = ∓3 D) CHART
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Kepler (1604) & Donders/Snellen (1862) human eye ray-tracing diagram (cornea ~43 dioptres + crystalline lens ~15–20 dioptres = ~58–60 dioptres total refractive power focusing at 24 mm axial length; ±1 mm axial error = ∓3 dioptres of myopia/hyperopia) on period paper
teach_overlay.scale: every single millimetre your eyeball grows too long throws your focus off by three dioptres — meaning a difference smaller than the thickness of a British pound coin turns a sharp street sign across the road into a blurry smudge
teach_overlay.who_card: Ibn al-Haytham (c. 965–c. 1040) — Arab mathematician and physicist · Johannes Kepler (1571–1630) — German astronomer and mathematician · Christoph Scheiner (1573–1650) — German Jesuit physicist and astronomer · Thomas Young (1773–1829) — British physician and physicist · Franciscus Cornelis Donders (1818–1889) — Dutch ophthalmologist and physiologist · Herman Snellen (1834–1908) — Dutch ophthalmologist

plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period parchment, an inked Herman Snellen (1862 Probebuchstaben zur Bestimmung der Sehschärfe, Utrecht) 5×5 Grid Optotype & 5-Arcminute Visual Acuity Angle diagram shows the big 'E' at 20 feet (6 metres) subtending 5 minutes of arc (1/12th of 1 degree), with each stroke and gap subtending 1 minute of arc to match the spacing of cone photoreceptors in the human fovea.

teach_overlay.label: 1862 HERMAN SNELLEN (UTRECHT): 5×5 GRID OPTOTYPE & 5-ARCMINUTE (1 ARCMINUTE STROKE AT 20 FT / 6 M) 20/20 VISUAL ACUITY CHART
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Herman Snellen (1862) 20/200 to 20/20 visual acuity chart geometry (5 arcminutes letter height, 1 arcminute stroke width at 20 feet / 6 metres) on period paper
teach_overlay.scale: reading the 20/20 line on Snellen's eye chart from twenty feet away requires your eye to distinguish gaps of just one-sixtieth of a degree — like spotting the space between two fingers held up from the far end of a tennis court
